title: Paytm Founder's Entity to Sell Nearly 5% Stake in Half-Billion Dollar Block Deal
excerpt: Resilient Asset Management, fully owned by Vijay Shekhar Sharma, plans to offload a 4.98% stake in One97 Communications with Antfin retaining the economic proceeds.
body:
• Resilient Asset Management, wholly owned by Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma, has proposed selling up to 4.98% stake in One97 Communications
  • The block trade is valued at approximately ₹4,895 crore (~$528 million) at a floor price of ₹1,535.10 per share
  • China's Antfin will retain the economic value of the sale proceeds under the original 2023 transfer arrangement
  • Sharma's direct 9.03% shareholding in Paytm remains unchanged by this transaction

Paytm's parent company One97 Communications disclosed on Monday that Resilient Asset Management, a Netherlands-based entity fully owned by founder and CEO Vijay Shekhar Sharma, has proposed selling up to a 4.98% stake in the fintech company through a block deal, according to Reuters.

Deal Structure and Pricing

The floor price for the block trade has been set at ₹1,535.10 per share, a 2.9% discount to Paytm's closing price of ₹1,580.20 on Monday, Moneycontrol reported citing sources. At this price, the stake sale would be valued at approximately ₹4,895 crore, or roughly $528 million based on Reuters calculations using Paytm's last close.

Paytm shares ended the trading session 1.4% lower on Monday ahead of the anticipated deal.

The Antfin Connection

The sale traces back to a 2023 restructuring of Paytm's ownership. In August 2023, Antfin — the Netherlands-based arm of China's Ant Group, an Alibaba affiliate — transferred a 10.2% stake in One97 Communications to Resilient Asset Management. Under that arrangement, Resilient obtained ownership and voting rights, while Antfin received optionally convertible debentures and retained the economic value of the shares.

"The proposed deal will not change Sharma's direct shareholding in the company. Antfin will retain the value of the proceeds from the proposed block trade."

— One97 Communications, exchange filing

This means that while Sharma's entity is the seller of record, the financial proceeds effectively flow to Antfin. The deal represents another step in the gradual unwinding of Chinese ownership in India's most prominent fintech company.

Antfin's Exit Timeline

Antfin has been systematically reducing its exposure to Paytm over the past three years. The Chinese entity held a 27.9% stake when Paytm filed for its IPO in 2021. After the 2023 transfer to Resilient, Antfin's direct holding fell to 13.5%. A further 4% block sale in May 2025 for ₹2,103 crore brought the stake down to about 5.85%, and Antfin's final 5.84% stake was offloaded in a ₹3,803 crore block deal arranged by Goldman Sachs and Citigroup.

With this latest sale of shares held through Resilient, the last residual economic interest tied to the original Chinese investment is being monetized.

Impact on Paytm's Cap Table

After this transaction, Sharma's direct stake of 9.03% in Paytm remains intact, but Resilient's holding — which once stood at 10.2% — will drop to roughly 5.2%. Paytm remains a professionally managed company with no identified promoter under Indian securities law, which requires a shareholding above 25% for promoter classification.

What's Next

The block deal is expected to be executed on Tuesday. For Paytm, the steady exit of legacy Chinese ownership could help clear a lingering regulatory overhang, particularly around its pending payment aggregator license. Analysts have noted that reducing foreign strategic ownership strengthens the company's positioning with Indian regulators at a time when Paytm is reporting improved fundamentals, including its first-ever quarterly core business profit.
nri_angle: The unwinding of Chinese ownership in India's largest fintech company is closely watched by NRI investors tracking Paytm's regulatory trajectory and stock performance.
